out_of_scope_rules: Third party infrastructure and redirects are out of scope and not eligible for bounty.
Temporary Out-of-Scope (root cause analysis in progress): Cache Poisoning DoS
DoS/DDoS attacks or brute force attacks (e.g. GQL alias overloading, GQL query depth)
Bypassing rate-limits or the non-existence of rate-limits (also NOT a valid finding)
Subdomain takeover, banner grabbing/version disclosure, missing security headers
Verbose messages/files/directory listings without disclosing sensitive information
CORS misconfiguration on non-sensitive endpoints, username enumeration, missing cookie flags
Reflected-XSS without demonstrable impact, self-XSS, CSRF with no/low impact, clickjacking without impact
API key disclosure without proven business impact; disclosed/misconfigured API keys (Maps, DD Monitoring, etc.)
Blind SSRF without proven business impact (pingbacks insufficient); HTTP request smuggling without proven impact
Host header injection without proven business impact; CSV injection; email spoofing/SPF/DMARC/DKIM
Reports that state software is out of date/vulnerable without a proof-of-concept
Vulnerabilities only in software that no longer receives security updates
Theoretical issues with no realistic exploit scenario
Mobile: no cert pinning, jailbreak/root detection, obfuscation, pasteboard/clipboard leakage, path disclosure in binary, etc.
Zero-days in in-scope assets within 14 days of a public patch may be reported but are usually not bounty-eligible
